answer: Each identity lays one cable along the corridor from the wharf and locks a 60-credit bond on that cable. The ferrous cable carries a key signal the auditor tests against the cable map; two keys on one cable, or a depth below the map, burns the bond. In the grove at the corridor's end, each new cable goes deeper to clear earlier cables, so the k-th fee is 20+6(k-1) credits: the first 20, the 1000th 6014, and 1000 fakes pay 3,017,000 plus 60,000 locked. A cable-sharing ring fails the signal test and loses both bonds. An honest operator lays one cable, pays 20, and recovers the bond if clean.
